verdicts.quote: a group of people or words
verdicts.reason: This is imprecise: a line can be a row of people, but a line of writing is not simply a group of words.
A row is specifically an arrangement next to each other, whereas a line may also extend one behind another; this is not a dependable synonym for the full sense.
This is chiefly British English; the usual American term is clothesline, so it needs a British label or replacement.
This also has the common figurative meaning of behaving unacceptably, given separately as a phrase, so it is ambiguous without a physical-boundary qualifier.

verdicts.quote: The house has been in the family line for many years.
verdicts.reason: Family line does not naturally mean a family's continuing ownership of a house; the example does not illustrate the stated sense.

reviewers.summary: The entry is broadly accurate and well structured, but it needs an abstract-boundary sense for line and a replacement for the unnatural family-line example. Several smaller issues concern precision and regional or ambiguous collocations.
The entry for line (noun) is exceptionally thorough, accurate, and fully compliant with all lexicographical house rules.
